correctness.rationale: For nu=d/2>=1 the unnormalized annulus transform is (2pi)^nu t^-nu[J_nu(t)-a^nu J_nu(at)]. H_nu(t)=t^nu J_nu(t) has H_nu prime=t^nu J_(nu-1)(t). The energy E=t^(2nu)(J_(nu-1)^2+J_nu^2) has derivative (4nu-2)t^(2nu-1)J_(nu-1)^2, strictly positive after integration. This forces exactly one simple zero per bracket between successive J_(nu-1) zeros and fixes the sign of D=J_(nu-1)(tau)-a^(nu+1)J_(nu-1)(a*tau). Differentiate H_nu(tau)=H_nu(a*tau): tau prime=a^nu*tau*J_(nu-1)(a*tau)/D; (a*tau) prime=tau*J_(nu-1)(tau)/D>0. Endpoint limits are a*tau ->0 and j_(nu-1,k). It crosses exactly the earlier k-1 simple Bessel zeros, each giving a simple zero of tau prime. Bracket monotonicity and unequal successive extrema establish the unique level intersections. No finite sample substitutes for this all-k/d proof. The original bracket and endpoint argument was independently checked against its earlier published full text.
